items.title: The UN System — Organs, Council & Reform
items.body:
## United Nations

- Founded **24 October 1945** (UN Charter); HQ **New York**; **193 members**; official languages 6 (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish).
- **Six principal organs**: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Secretariat, ICJ (The Hague), and the **Trusteeship Council** (suspended 1994).

## Security Council

- **15 members = 5 permanent (P5) + 10 non-permanent** (two-year terms, elected by the UNGA).
- **P5: USA, UK, France, Russia, China** — each holds the **veto**.
- **Reform**: the **G4 (India, Japan, Germany, Brazil)** seek permanent seats; the African bloc's demand is the **Ezulwini Consensus**. India is a strong claimant but **not** yet a permanent member.

## Secretary-General

- **António Guterres** (Portugal), in office since Jan 2017, second term to 2026; appointed by the UNGA on the UNSC's recommendation.

## Specialised agencies (mandates & HQs)

| Agency | HQ | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| WHO | Geneva | Health |
| UNESCO | Paris | Education, science, culture |
| ILO | Geneva | Labour |
| FAO | Rome | Food & agriculture |
| ICJ | The Hague | UN judicial organ (15 judges, Pres. Yuji Iwasawa) |
keyPoints: UN founded 24 October 1945; HQ New York; 193 members; six principal organs.
Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 — not currently active.
UNSC = 5 permanent (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) + 10 non-permanent (2-year terms).
G4 = India, Japan, Germany, Brazil seek permanent UNSC seats; India is not yet a permanent member.
António Guterres (Portugal) has been UN Secretary-General since January 2017.
HQs: WHO & ILO Geneva, UNESCO Paris, FAO Rome, ICJ The Hague (President Yuji Iwasawa, Japan).
items.mnemonic: G4 seat-seekers = 'JBIG' → Japan, Brazil, India, Germany.
items.source: United Nations (un.org); ICJ (icj-cij.org); agency sites — verified Sep 2026

items.title: Bretton Woods Twins & the WTO
items.body:
## Origins

- The **IMF** and **World Bank** were created at the **Bretton Woods** conference (1944); both are headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**
- By convention the **IMF MD is European** and the **World Bank President is American**.

## IMF

- Ensures **monetary stability** and provides **balance-of-payments** support; ~191 members.
- **Managing Director: Kristalina Georgieva** (Bulgaria), since 2019 (second term from 2024).

## World Bank Group (5 arms)

| Arm | Role |
|---|---|
| IBRD | Loans to middle-income governments |
| IDA | Concessional credit to poorest states |
| IFC | Private-sector financing |
| MIGA | Political-risk guarantees |
| ICSID | Investment dispute settlement |

- **IBRD + IDA = "the World Bank"**. **President: Ajay Banga** (Indian-American), since June 2023.

## WTO

- Succeeded the **GATT on 1 January 1995**; HQ **Geneva**; ~166 members; adds a **binding dispute-settlement** system.
- **Director-General: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala** (Nigeria) — first woman and first African DG, since 2021 (second term).
keyPoints: IMF and World Bank were both born at Bretton Woods (1944), HQ Washington D.C.
IMF Managing Director = Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria); World Bank President = Ajay Banga.
World Bank = IBRD + IDA; the Group also has IFC (private sector), MIGA (guarantees), ICSID (disputes).
WTO replaced GATT on 1 January 1995; HQ Geneva; has binding dispute settlement.
WTO Director-General = Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria), first woman and first African to hold the post.
items.mnemonic: World Bank arms 'I-I-I-M-I' = IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID.
items.source: IMF (imf.org); World Bank (worldbank.org); WTO (wto.org) — verified Sep 2026

items.title: Multilateral Development Banks — ADB, AIIB, NDB
items.body:
## Asian Development Bank (ADB)

- Founded **1966**; HQ **Manila, Philippines**; 68 members; Japan & USA are the largest shareholders.
- **President always Japanese by convention — Masato Kanda** (since Feb 2025, succeeding Masatsugu Asakawa).

## Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)

- China-proposed; operational **2016**; HQ **Beijing**; 100+ members; funds infrastructure.
- **President: Zou Jiayi** (China), since January 2026 (succeeded founding President **Jin Liqun**).

## New Development Bank (NDB)

- The **BRICS bank** — Fortaleza Declaration 2014, operational 2015; HQ **Shanghai**.
- **President: Dilma Rousseff** (former Brazilian President), since 2023; presidency rotates among founders.
- New members include Egypt, UAE and Bangladesh.

## Quick contrast

| Bank | Founded | HQ | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADB | 1966 | Manila | Masato Kanda |
| AIIB | 2016 | Beijing | Zou Jiayi |
| NDB | 2014/15 | Shanghai | Dilma Rousseff |
keyPoints: ADB founded 1966, HQ Manila; President (always Japanese) is Masato Kanda since Feb 2025.
AIIB operational 2016, HQ Beijing; President Zou Jiayi succeeded founding head Jin Liqun in Jan 2026.
NDB is the BRICS bank, HQ Shanghai; President Dilma Rousseff since 2023.
AIIB and NDB are both China-hosted but distinct — only the NDB is the BRICS bank.
India is a founding member of ADB, AIIB and NDB.

items.title: Regional & Plurilateral Groupings + Export-Control Regimes
items.body:
## Regional organisations

| Body | Founded | HQ | Members |
|---|---|---|---|
| SAARC | 1985 | Kathmandu | 8 |
| ASEAN | 1967 | Jakarta | 10 |
| BIMSTEC | 1997 | Dhaka | 7 |
| EU | 1993 | Brussels | 27 |

## Plurilateral groupings (India's role)

- **G20**: India held the **presidency in 2023 (New Delhi Declaration)**; the **African Union was admitted as a permanent member** at that summit. **G7** is a separate advanced-economy club (India not a member).
- **BRICS**: expanded from 2024 (added **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE**; **Indonesia** joined 2025).
- **SCO**: India became a **full member in 2017**; HQ Beijing.
- **QUAD**: India, USA, Japan, Australia. **I2U2**: India, Israel, UAE, USA.

## Export-control regimes (India's status)

- **MTCR** — joined **2016**; **Wassenaar Arrangement** — **2017**; **Australia Group** — **2018**.
- **NSG** — India's membership bid **remains blocked** (China objects on the NPT issue).

## Climate fora

- **UNFCCC (1992)** is the climate treaty; the **Paris Agreement (2015)** sits under it; the **IPCC** (set up by **WMO + UNEP**) provides the scientific assessments.
keyPoints: HQs: SAARC Kathmandu, ASEAN Jakarta, BIMSTEC Dhaka, EU Brussels.
India held the G20 presidency in 2023; the African Union became a permanent G20 member at the New Delhi summit.
India became a full SCO member in 2017; QUAD = India, USA, Japan, Australia; I2U2 = India, Israel, UAE, USA.
India joined MTCR (2016), Wassenaar (2017) and Australia Group (2018) but NOT the NSG.
IPCC was established by WMO and UNEP; the Paris Agreement (2015) operates under the UNFCCC (1992).
items.mnemonic: India's export-club years: MTCR-16, Wassenaar-17, Australia Group-18 (16→17→18), NSG still pending.
items.source: MEA (mea.gov.in); SAARC/ASEAN/BIMSTEC/EU sites; IPCC (ipcc.ch); UNFCCC (unfccc.int) — verified Sep 2026

items.title: PYQ Precision — Reports, Memberships, HQs & OECD
items.body:
## 'Report published by' (high-frequency match)

| Report | Body |
|---|---|
| Human Development Report | **UNDP** |
| World Investment Report | **UNCTAD** |
| Global Competitiveness Report | **WEF** (non-UN, Davos) |
| Global Financial Stability Report / World Economic Outlook | **IMF** |
| World Development Report | **World Bank** |
| State of World Population | **UNFPA** |

## India: member vs not

- **Member**: UN, IMF, World Bank, WTO, ADB, **AIIB** (2nd-largest shareholder), NDB.
- **NOT a member**: **OECD** (Paris), **OPEC** (Vienna), ICSID.

## HQ traps

- **Vienna**: IAEA, OPEC, UNIDO, CTBTO. **Geneva**: WHO, ILO, WTO, WMO, WIPO. **Rome**: FAO/WFP/IFAD. **Nairobi**: UNEP/UN-Habitat. **The Hague**: ICJ & ICC.

## OECD & WTO

- **BEPS** = OECD/G20 anti-tax-avoidance framework; **Two-Pillar** global minimum tax (**15%**).
- **TFA** concluded at WTO **Bali (2013)**; **Masala bonds** = offshore rupee bonds (IFC pioneered).
keyPoints: HDR = UNDP; World Investment Report = UNCTAD; Global Competitiveness Report = WEF (non-UN); GFSR/WEO = IMF.
India is NOT a member of the OECD or OPEC, but IS a member of AIIB, NDB, ADB, IMF, World Bank and WTO.
Vienna hosts IAEA and OPEC; Geneva hosts WHO/ILO/WTO; Rome hosts FAO.
BEPS is the OECD/G20 framework; the Two-Pillar deal sets a 15% global minimum tax.
The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement was agreed at Bali (2013); Masala bonds are offshore rupee bonds (IFC).
